note: City of Crawford municipal park along the White River (a narrow stream here). Four electric pads in the park proper, which campers say back onto the river, plus three non-pad electric sites near the White River Wacipi arbor and dry camping throughout the park complex. Restroom seasonal, no showers. The bridge at the main entrance is posted 5 tons, under EKKO's weight: campers (2024, April 2026) come in instead by the dirt road around the outside of the park to the back entrance. Firsthand reviews report 29-34 ft RVs (incl. a 32-ft Class C) at the electric sites. Frequent BNSF trains sound their horns day and night. Camping at the rodeo grounds goes through the Old West Trail Rodeo Board. --Claude
summary: The City of Crawford's own park page confirms FCFS, no reservations, 14-night max, $20 electric / $10 dry, dump and water hydrants (page undated; an Aug 2024 camper paid the same). Fees added (none stored): 10-20. Booking and facilities now manual. Phone and website were missing: city page and City Hall numbers found. Waterfront lead (up, to creekside) from two camper reports that the four pads back onto the White River; pads not located on imagery, so not waterfront stays. 5-ton bridge caveat kept.

ACCESS / WEIGHT (criteria caveat, kept): the main entrance bridge is posted 5 tons (camper reports Aug 2024 and Apr 25, 2026), below EKKO's ~11,000 lb GVWR (memory: a 5-ton limit excludes). Both reviewers came in or left by an unposted dirt road 'all along the outside of the park' to a back entrance, so the park stays reachable; the note says so. The city's page says nothing about the bridge.

WATERFRONT LEAD (up, not waterfront -> creekside?, not changed): a May 2025 Campendium reviewer: 'Water and power at four campsites that back up directly on the White river'; an Apr 25, 2026 reviewer: '#2 can reach the water.' On z19 imagery the White River in the park is a narrow stream (~3-7 m channel, a small footbridge) under heavy cottonwood canopy, so any on-water value would be creekside (under ~30 m). I could not pick out the four pads under the trees, OSM was unavailable, and no official site map exists, so the gate is not cleared; not waterfront stays (stored evidence calls it a 'vegetated/dry creek channel').

RATE DATING (weak): the city page carries no date; the $20/$10 figures match an Aug 2024 camper report and the current NW Nebraska tourism listing. A Campendium summary in search results mentioned a $25 'last paid' in 2025 that I did not see on the page.
